candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis V.24 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 362 AD)

'And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him' Ephrem takes as central to the entire Tewahedo theological imagination, since Enoch is the canonical author of the Mäṣḥafä Hēnok (1 Enoch). The 'walking with God' Ephrem reads as the Syriac patristic ideal of continual conscious communion — the same standard upheld for Noah (6:9) and re-articulated for Abraham (17:1). The translation ('God took him') Ephrem takes literally: Enoch did not die in the ordinary mode but was assumed bodily into divine presence. Together with the parallel translation of Elijah (2 Kings 2:11), this establishes the Old Testament's witness to bodily glorification before the universal resurrection. Tewahedo eschatology preserves both translations with particular weight, since Enoch's translated state grounds the authority of the Mäṣḥafä Hēnok he composed.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis V.29 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 362 AD)

Lamech's naming of Noah — 'This same shall comfort us (yenahamenu) concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the LORD hath cursed' — Ephrem reads as prophetic anticipation grounded in pre-flood corruption. Noah's name (the Hebrew root n-w-h, to rest/comfort) Ephrem takes as etymologically programmatic: Noah will be the one through whom the post-flood relief is mediated, the cursed ground (Gen 3:17) being either washed clean or replaced by new earth in the renewal that follows the flood. Ephrem reads Lamech's hope as proleptically Christological: every Old Testament expectation of comfort-mediated-by-a-righteous-one ultimately points beyond itself to Christ as the true Comforter. The Tewahedo Synaxarium preserves Noah on the 10th of Magabit as a type of Christ.
